     """
     Capitalize all the words and replace some characters in the string to
     create a nicer looking title. :func:`titleize` is meant for creating pretty
-    output.
+    output. Words written in all capitals, such as acronyms, are kept as they
+    are.
 
     Examples::
 
@@ -370,13 +371,30 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       'The Man Without A Past'
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
 
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    words = _underscore_keep_case(word)
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
-        humanize(underscore(word)).title()
+        humanize(words.lower()).title()
     )
+    # The title has the words of ``words`` in the same order (humanize() may
+    # drop a trailing "id"), so put back the ones written in all capitals.
+    # Checking that the two words match guards against the rare Unicode case
+    # mappings that split a word in two.
+    originals: typing.Iterator[str] = iter(re.findall(r"[^\W_]+", words))
+
+    def keep_capitals(match: typing.Match[str]) -> str:
+        original = next(originals, '')
+        titled = match.group()
+        if original.isupper() and original.casefold() == titled.casefold():
+            return original
+        return titled
+
+    return re.sub(r"[^\W_]+", keep_capitals, title)
